The past year I've discovered a sustainable diet and exercise plan that has been very good for overall health and athletics. I recommend you try it out and adapt it to your own personal needs.

First, a little background. My girlfriend (at the time) and I had just moved in together and one of our first conversations was what were our health and fitness goals and how could we support each other in them. We're both quite athletic climbers and cyclists so our goals were similar: increase muscle mass, lose a bit of fat, climb better, cycle better, and achieve perfect blood work for our annual physicals.

Food was critical to this. We ate very high protein and fat diets with virtually no simple carbs besides fruit. We also would fast one to two days per week on average. Every morning, one of us would make a breakfast that typically had 2-4 eggs, a few cups of greens, onion, garlic, peppers, sausage, and 12 oz of whole milk each. Lunch was leftover dinner and dinner was a home cooked meal that featured mostly meat, veggies, beans, lentils, and whole grains. We never ate bread or junk food, except as an occasional treat. For meat, it was mostly beef, pork, and mutton. Snacks were fruit, veggies, nuts, and cheese. We made sure to get plenty of fiber.

We consumed a lot of dairy, red meat, and eggs. We also saw our cholesterol and triglycerides hit breath takingly good levels. The satiation from these helped my girl kick her carb snacking habit dead and she lost about 10lbs of fat. We both saw climbing gains from all the good protein too. Furthermore, as our bodies adapted to the lower carb diet, our endurance cycling improved and we required fewer sugary snacks on long bike rides to keep the energy up.

The fast days as a method of calorie restriction helped us to lose fat and build muscle at the same time. During much of the week, there was extra energy to build muscle but the weekly energy intake was low enough to burn fat week over week. I think the fasting + low carb is the real trick to this diet.

Exercise was also huge. I'll look at our typical work week first. Mornings were usually just high intensity fucking and biking to work (30min). Throughout the day, we'd take walks together and usually get a few miles in. On the way home, we'd often hit the trails and do 30-60min of moderate off-road trail biking (on our commuters). After dinner we'd often either go for a longer bike ride or hit the climbing gym for a couple hours.

Bike commuting was usually two to three days per work week. The evening bike rides were also two to three days per workweek. Climbing was two work nights. The work week usually had around 12 hours of exercise.

Weekends were very free form. Often we'd either be camping/hiking the whole time or if we stayed at home we'd do at least three hours per day of exercise (usually cycling or climbing, but rowing and others were common too). All in all, the typical weekend was 6-10 hours of physical activity.

I know it sounds intense, but if you do this you'll feel better than you ever have in your life and be so happy. Highly recommend it.

tl;dr: ate a lot of animal fat and protein along with very few carbs and a fast day to get massive health gains while exercising 18-22 hours per week.
